skill.name: agent-manager-skill
skill.description: Guides users in managing multiple local CLI agents with tmux sessions, monitoring, task assignment, and scheduled recurring work.
skill.summary: Coordinates local CLI agents through tmux sessions, monitoring commands, task assignment, and cron-friendly workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The shell execution alerts are Markdown examples and inline command references, not code executed by the skill. The hardcoded GitHub clone URL is a real low-severity supply-chain and network concern because installation depends on fetching an external repository.

remediation.suggestion: Document why the external GitHub repository is required, pin a commit or release, and verify it matches the marketplace source.

remediation.issue: Command examples rely on local tooling
remediation.suggestion: Keep the commands as explicit user-run examples and avoid adding automatic install or execution hooks.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 21 uses Markdown inline code for the skill name in installation prose. It does not execute a shell command or interpolate user input.
Line 23 starts a fenced bash documentation block. The block shows a user-run setup command and is not executable code inside the skill.
Line 25 closes the fenced Markdown block. The backticks are formatting markers, not Ruby or shell execution syntax.
Line 29 opens a bash examples block for agent-manager commands. These are documentation examples and no automatic command runner is present.
Line 37 closes the Markdown command block. The backticks are static formatting and cannot execute commands.
Line 41 uses inline code to name required local tools. It does not call those tools or pass data to a shell.
Line 24 instructs users to clone a hardcoded external GitHub repository during setup. This is visible documentation, but it still creates a supply-chain dependency on remote network content.

low_findings.title: Hardcoded URL
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 24 instructs users to clone a hardcoded external GitHub repository during setup. This is visible documentation, but it still creates a supply-chain dependency on remote network content.

content.value_statement: Running several local agents can become hard to track across terminals and logs. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a clear workflow for tmux sessions, monitoring, assignment, and scheduling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use a tmux-based manager for local CLI agents.
Provides setup guidance that clones the external agent-manager repository.
Lists doctor, list, start, monitor, and assign command patterns.
Shows how to send a task to a named agent using the manager script.
Documents prerequisites for tmux, python3, and an agents directory.
limitations: It does not include the agent-manager implementation files.
It depends on an external GitHub repository for the actual scripts.
It assumes tmux and python3 are available in the local environment.
It does not validate agent output or replace project-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Local Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Start separate CLI agents in tmux and assign focused work to each session.

use_cases.title: Monitor Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: List active agents, follow output, and check local execution state from one command workflow.

use_cases.title: Schedule Recurring Agent Tasks
use_cases.description: Use cron-friendly commands to run maintenance or review work on a recurring schedule.

prompt_templates.title: Check Agent Manager Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to check whether my workspace is ready. Show the doctor command and explain what to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Start and Watch One Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to start agent EMP_0001 and monitor its output. Include the exact command sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Assign a Focused Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to assign a maintenance task to EMP_0002. Format the task text for a here-document.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scheduled Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-manager skill to design a cron-friendly workflow for recurring repository maintenance across multiple local agents.

output_examples.input: Check whether the manager is usable in this workspace.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the doctor command, lists required tools, and explains which local checks should pass before starting agents.

output_examples.input: Start EMP_0001 and follow its output.
output_examples.output: The assistant provides a short command sequence to start the named agent and monitor its tmux-backed session.

output_examples.input: Create a recurring agent maintenance plan.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines a cron-friendly workflow with agent listing, task assignment, monitoring, and project-specific validation steps.

best_practices: Verify the external repository source before cloning or running scripts.
Run the doctor command before starting or assigning work to agents.
Keep task prompts scoped, auditable, and tied to local project validation.
anti_patterns: Do not run external scripts before reviewing their source and permissions.
Do not assign broad or unclear tasks to long-running agents.
Do not treat agent output as complete without tests or human review.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It guides local CLI agent management through tmux sessions, monitoring commands, task assignment, and scheduled workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill include the manager scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill points users to an external GitHub repository that contains the implementation.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires tmux and python3 in the local environment.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to clone the linked repository?
faq.answer: Review the linked repository, pin a trusted revision, and follow your organization policy before running its scripts.

faq.question: Does it replace testing or review?
faq.answer: No. Agent output still needs project-specific validation, tests, and human review where appropriate.
